frozen_initial_policy.mechanism: Band gap is set by anion p to cation s/d separation. Fluoride/oxide ligands give deep, localized p bands and strong ionicity, while empty d-block or lanthanide 4f states sit high; transition-metal chalcogenides add low-lying d bands that collapse the gap.
failure_conditions: LaF3-type fluoride scores below the transition-metal chalcogenide, refuting the ionicity prior.
Hybrid oxide complex exceeds the fluoride anchor, indicating molecular-crystal effects dominate.
All three outcomes fall within a narrow band, showing decision schema lacks resolving power.

previous_llm_decision.updated_hypothesis: Wide PBE gaps come from f0/d0 ionic fluoride lattices; Zr-cluster chlorides with occupied metal-metal d states collapse gaps, while Ca-dominated mixed fluorides should approach the LaF3 anchor.
evidence_for: Fluorides dominate observed target highs (F18La6 = 75.5); this is a Ca/Y fluoride-rich lattice.
GP rank 1 with UCB 82.6 and low mean_z, consistent with ionic wide-gap chemistry.
evidence_against: Nd/Ho 4f states can pin mid-gap levels in PBE, as seen in Nd complex (59.1).
Eligible alternatives are Zr6Cl12 clusters with metal-metal d bands expected near zero gap.
previous_llm_decision.reasoning_summary: Among the three eligible rows, only the mixed alkaline-earth/rare-earth fluoride has the ionic F-dominant lattice that produced every high observed outcome; Zr-cluster chlorides carry conducting d states.
